A strong critique names one specific assumption, explains how reality may violate it, and states how the conclusion could change. For stopping distance, one may criticize the assumptions of fixed reaction time and uniform braking conditions: fatigue, wet pavement, tire wear, and slope can all increase stopping distance, so the fitted model should be recalibrated for those conditions. For the medication model, one may criticize the assumption of one uniform patient response: metabolism, body mass, kidney function, and interactions can shift both the peak time and concentration. Full credit requires the assumption, its consequence, and a proposed measurement or model improvement.
